from.place: ## Proof, sentence 'They are acyclic by [lem-sc-zero-generic-acyclic]': the kernel and cokernel of the unit need the version for generically vanishing sections without a torsion hypothesis.

title: Acyclicity for generically vanishing etale sheaves on a curve
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $C$ an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves]. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Assume that for every etale $C$-scheme $V$ and every section $s\in G(V)$ there is an etale covering $\{V_a\to V\}$ in $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] such that for every $a$ there is a nonempty affine open $U_a\subset C$ with inclusion $j_a:U_a\to C$ and the image of $s|_{V_a}$ under the adjunction unit $G\to j_{a*}j_a^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] equal to zero on $V_a$. Then $H^q(C_{\Et},G)=0$ for every $q>0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No torsion hypothesis on $G$ is imposed.

source.place: ## Proof, acyclicity sentence; precise Lean statement and docstring: WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/GenericComparison.lean, AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.subsingleton_H_of_genericVanishing, lines 140-232

proof.text: For every nonempty affine open U, form the kernel K_U of the adjunction unit G \to j_{U*}j_U^{-1}G. Compatibility of the units for nested affine opens gives the transition maps, and the generic-vanishing covering hypothesis makes the canonical map from the filtered colimit of the K_U to G both monic and locally surjective; hence it is an isomorphism.

For each U, the inverse image of K_U on U is zero: after pulling the unit back along j_U, the left triangle identity makes the resulting map an isomorphism, so its kernel is zero. The complement of U in the integral curve is a finite set of closed points with separably closed residue fields. Therefore the finite-support acyclicity lemma applies to K_U and gives H^q(C,K_U)=0 for every q>0.

The curve C is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so filtered colimits of abelian etale sheaves commute with H^q(C,-). Applying the canonical colimit isomorphism from the first step gives H^q(C,G) as the filtered colimit of the groups H^q(C,K_U).

source.place: Lemma 03Q5 (filtered colimits and etale cohomology), as used for the curve in the Lean proof

proof.text: Every group in that filtered colimit is zero in positive degree by the second step, so the colimit is zero. Hence H^q(C,G)=0 for every q>0.

theorem subsingleton_H_of_genericVanishing
    (G : Sheaf C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hG : ∀ (V : C.Etale) (s : G.obj.obj (op V)),
      C.genericVanishingSieve G s ∈ C.smallEtaleTopology V) (i : ℕ) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H G (i + 1))
lean.note: Exact source theorem, GenericComparison.lean:146–232. Inherited binders: {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [IsIntegral C]. The covering genericVanishingSieve is exactly the local affine-open unit-vanishing hypothesis; i+1 ranges over all positive degrees. Sheaf.H is the source cohomology convention accepted by def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, with its derived-global-sections comparison deferred to stage 3. The existing proof is transitively sorried, so this record is a stage-2 statement reuse, not a stage-3 proof claim.
